loop.authoritative_status: Query the runtime get_goal tool; this file is not a liveness receipt.

commit_policy: Commit every tested task and integrate reviewed increments into the Moriarty main branch. Preserve raw receipts and runtime checkpoint exports. Never commit credentials or transient database files.

sprints.name: Terminology and intent theorem freeze
sprints.requirement: Freeze definitions, observation model, hard predicates, assumptions, and the candidate correctness-of-intent theorem. Do not change Core.

sprints.name: Core and intent semantic alternatives
sprints.requirement: Specify and model-check the agreement-Core-plus-intent, intent-Core, two-calculus, and library-only options. Select one or stop.

sprints.name: Semantic motions
sprints.requirement: Decide each constructor, type, effect, authorization, visibility, cancellation, partial-fill, and composition motion. Publish a new scope digest only for accepted changes.

sprints.name: Mechanized reference semantics
sprints.requirement: Select the normative environment. Implement executable semantics and the first theorem spine. Establish independent conformance.

sprints.name: Surface and certifying elaboration
sprints.requirement: Specify and implement typed surface, elaboration, canonical Core, source maps, and type, bound, visibility, and capability certificates.

sprints.name: Compact compiler and translation validation
sprints.requirement: Implement one shared backend for multiple applications. Preserve readable Compact, artifact identity, differential traces, and mutation evidence.

sprints.name: Intent verifier and CAKE boundaries
sprints.requirement: Implement intent, resolver, solver-plan, and settlement boundary contracts. Make the client reject unauthorized plans before signing.

sprints.name: ERC compatibility profiles
sprints.requirement: Implement or reject adapters through evidence. Preserve every semantic mismatch and current standards revision.

sprints.name: Proof-of-intent vertical slice
sprints.requirement: Link mechanized semantics, translation evidence, real proof verification, plan verification, signing, and observed settlement for one application.

sprints.name: Complete developer interface
sprints.requirement: Reconcile and implement the minimum safety spine. Validate all API and data contracts across supported environments.

sprints.name: ACTUS source lock and conformance harness
sprints.requirement: Freeze the public ACTUS source, repository, license, taxonomy, and fixture inventories. Implement lossless schemas, discovery, exact numeric parsing, ordered full-field comparison, coverage manifests, and negative controls.

sprints.name: ACTUS typed packages and independent semantics
sprints.requirement: Implement all 18 executable contract types as typed surface packages over shared abstractions. Run all 277 fixtures through two independent semantics implementations. Process any proven Core expressivity gap as a semantic motion instead of adding a product-specific escape hatch.

sprints.name: ACTUS shared compilation and backend correspondence
sprints.requirement: Elaborate and compile all 277 fixtures through canonical Core and the general Compact backend. Preserve differential traces, field-level results, source maps, resource bounds, adversarial cases, metamorphic cases, and mutation evidence. No excluded fixture can advance the sprint.

sprints.name: Adversarial conformance and audit
sprints.requirement: Run differential, property, fuzz, mutation, privacy, malicious solver, malicious Runtime, malicious prover, wallet, rollback, and ACTUS compatibility exercises.

sprints.name: Terminal decision
sprints.requirement: Decide language, library plus certifier, intent verifier only, or stop. Preserve dissent, evidence gaps, the ACTUS completion verdict, and the exact next scope.

release_gates.predicate: No unresolved ambiguity exists in normative syntax, typing, dynamics, observations, or canonical encoding.
Every deployable program has machine-checked finite lifetime and resource bounds.
Every accepted semantic motion has a proof delta, migration result, backend result, and negative test.
At least two independent semantics implementations pass every conformance vector, including every mandatory ACTUS vector.
Reference and generated backend agree on every required trace and effect projection, including every present ordered ACTUS result field.

Every adjacent lifecycle artifact binds its predecessor digest, domain, state, resolver and contract identity, upgrade state, assumptions, and version. The intent verifier rejects substitution, omission, equivocation, staleness, or any unauthorized objective, quote, authorization, resolution, plan, fee, disclosure, fill, fulfillment, and recovery mutation before its authority boundary.
Replay fails across network, contract, version, sequence, nonce, validity, and cancellation domains.
All public effects and private disclosures match the signed intent and approved manifests. Disclosure acceptance is distinct from effect authorization and cannot expand it.
Real proofs verify under pinned, approved, and digest-bound parameters.
Proof and ledger costs meet frozen application-specific budgets on named hardware and network versions.
Every security-critical compiler or verifier mutant is detected, or the survivor blocks release.
Build artifacts reproduce byte-for-byte on two independent clean builders.
No critical or high audit finding remains unresolved.

The SDK has stable errors, typed verification certificates, idempotency, version negotiation, asynchronous cancellation, partial-fill residuals, durable delivery deduplication, crash consistency, fill and payout separation, settlement levels, typed reversals, compensation, refund, and unavailable outcomes.
A compromised solver, Runtime, indexer, registry, or remote prover cannot create a signing request for extra effects.

The proof claim names every trusted compiler, circuit, verifier, parameter, ledger, wallet, oracle, relay, validator, treasury, custodian, and bridge assumption. Confidential profiles have a separate leakage theorem and trusted-computing-base statement.
At least two non-toy pilots, including the complete ACTUS benchmark, prefer Moriarty's assurance workflow to the audited Compact-library baseline.
If G05, G06, G09, G15, G17, or any ACTUS gate G19 through G24 fails, reduce scope or stop the language path.

The ACTUS source lock reproduces all public site and repository dispositions, the 32-row taxonomy, the 18 executable contract types, 276 contract fixtures, one analysis-date fixture, all licenses, and every known access limitation.
Discovery, lossless parsing, and execution cover all 277 mandatory ACTUS vectors. No vector is skipped, excluded, quarantined, marked as an expected failure, or hidden by an allowlist.

Two independent semantics implementations match every present ordered result field for every ACTUS vector under the frozen decimal, rounding, date, calendar, event-order, observation, and comparison rules.

Every ACTUS vector elaborates through the shared typed surface and canonical Core, compiles through the general Compact backend, matches the reference trace and effect projection, and stays within declared finite resource bounds. No fixture-specific or contract-specific compiler bypass exists.
Every one of the 32 ACTUS taxonomy rows has exactly one evidence-backed disposition. Only the 18 executable types with passing vectors count as implemented-and-vector-tested.

The release dossier uses ACTUS reference-vector compatibility, preserves attribution and license duties, identifies the private Java core as optional and unavailable unless authorized, states limitations, and makes no certification or endorsement claim.

limitations: Missing evidence is not a passed gate or a demonstrated infeasibility result.
Human pilot results require real participants. No contacting or recruiting people is authorized by this execution request.
Real proofs, approved parameters, ledger measurements, independent clean builders, and ACTUS coverage require their own preserved runs.
